body.p: The present amendment is responsive to the Office Action dated August 28, 2024 ("Office Action") and is timely filed within the shortened statutory period of three months for reply. Claims 1- 16 were pending in the application at the time of the Office Action. Claims 1-16 were rejected in the Office Action. Claims 1 and 6 have been amended. No new matter has been added by the foregoing amendments. In view of the foregoing amendments and the following remarks, reconsideration and withdrawal of the Examiner's rejections and a Notice of Allowance of all pending claims are earnestly solicited.

In the Office Action, the Examiner objected to the drawings under 37 C.F.R. § 1.83(a). More particularly, the Examiner contended that the features "second portion of the working structure, second sealed bulkhead, two lower openings" recited in the claims must be shown in the drawings or the features canceled from the claims. (See Office Action p. 2 Item 1.) Applicant respectfully traverses this objection for at least the following reasons.

The drawings illustrate a first portion 41 of the working structure 4 and the second portion 42 of the working structure 4 in FIGS. 3, 7-9. (See also Specification 11 [0057], [0059].) Thus, the drawings illustrate the second portion of the working structure configured to receive a vertical tail unit of the aircraft recited in claim 6, for example.

Likewise, the drawings illustrate a first sealed bulkhead 16 and second sealed bulkhead 17 separating the fuselage section T3 and the fuselage section T2 in FIG. 11. (See also Specification 1 [0061].) Thus, the drawings illustrate a second sealed bulkhead separating the third fuselage section
(T3) and the second fuselage section (T2) recited in claim 7, for example.

Finally, the drawings illustrate two lower openings 10 in a lower part of the fuselage section T3 in FIG. 6. (See also Specification 1 [0066].). Thus, the drawings illustrate two lower openings in a lower part of the third fuselage section (T3) recited in claim 11, for example. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the objection to the drawings are respectfully requested. Claim Rejections- 35 U.S.C. § 112

The Examiner rejected claims 6 and 7 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. Regarding claim 6, the Examiner contended that it is unclear what element does the feature "second portion of the working structure refer to." (See Office Action p. 3 Item 2.) In response, claim 6 has been amended

to depend from intervening claim 4. Claim 4 recites "a first portion of the working structure configured to receive the propulsion system or systems of the aircraft (AC)." FIG. 9 illustrates a first portion 41 and a second portion 42. (See also, Specification [ 0057], [0059], [0062].) The features "second portion of the working structure" of amended claim 6 are clear when read in light of the specification and the drawings.

Regarding claim 7, the Examiner contended that it is unclear what element does the feature "second sealed bulkhead" refer to. (See Office Action p. 3 Item 3.) Applicant traverses this rejection for at least the following reasons. The Specification describes that "the fuselage section T3 comprises a sealed bulkhead 16 separating the fuselage section T1 and the fuselage section T3," and that "[t]he fuselage section T3 further comprises a sealed bulkhead 17 separating the fuselage section T3 and the fuselage section T2." (Specification [0061]; see also FIG. 11.) Therefore, the feature "a second sealed bulkhead separating the third fuselage section (T3) and the second fuselage section (T2)" is clear when read in light of the specification and the drawings. Claim 7 and amended claim 6 comply with the statutory requirements of 35 U.S.C. § 112(b). Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) rejection of claims 6 and 7 are respectfully requested. Claim Rejections- 35 U.S.C. @ 102

The Examiner rejected claims 1-3 and 13-16 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 20080230654 Al to Velicki; Alexander et al. ("Velicki"). Applicant traverses this rejection for at least the following reasons.

The Examiner contended that Velicki discloses all of the features of claim 1. (See Office Action p. 4 Item 4.) It is respectfully submitted that the cited art fails to disclose every feature of amended claim 1, as set forth in detail below.

Amended claim 1 recites, inter alia, that "the first fuselage section (T1), the second fuselage section (T2), and the third fuselage section (T3) extend sequentially to one another along the first longitudinal axis (A)." Support for the amendment may be found throughout the specification, for example, in [0048], [0049], [0055], [0061], and the drawings, for example, in FIGS. 1, 3, 7, 11. No new matter has been added by this amendment.

The Examiner contended with reference to Velicki that the cockpit 526 constitutes the recited at least one first fuselage section, the continuous pressurized cabin 524 constitutes the recited second fuselage section and the section housing the supplemental saddle tanks 508A, 508B constitutes the

third fuselage section. (See Office Action p. 4 Item 4.) As can be seen from FIG. 5B of Velicki, the alleged second fuselage section (pressurized cabin 524) and the alleged third fuselage section (outboard sections of the cabin 524) are parallel to one another. In contrast, amended claim 1 recites that the first, second and third fuselage sections extend sequentially to one another along the first longitudinal axis (A). Velicki fails to disclose these features of amended claim 1. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) rejection of claim 1 are respectfully requested.

Claims 2, 3, and 13-16 ultimately depend from allowable base claim 1. At least by virtue of their dependence from claim 1, and in view of the reasons set forth above regarding amended claim 1, claims 2, 3, and 13-16 are also allowable over the cited art. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) rejection of claims 2, 3, and 13-16 are respectfully requested. Claim Rejections- 35 U.S.C . 103
The Examiner rejected claims 7 and 10-12 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Velicki. Applicant traverses this rejection for at least the following reasons.

Claims 7 and 10-12 depend from allowable base claim 1. At least by virtue of their dependence from claim 1, and in view of the reasons set forth above regarding amended claim 1, claims 7 and 10- 12 are also allowable over the cited art. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejection of claims 7 and 10-12 are respectfully requested.

The Examiner rejected claims 4-6, 8, and 9 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Velicki as applied to claims 1-3, 7 and 10-16, and further in view of French Patent Publication No. FR 3097201 Al to Thomas Matthieu et al. ("Matthieu"). Applicant traverses this rejection for at least the following reasons.

Claims 4-6, 8, and 9 ultimately depend from allowable base claim 1. At least by virtue of their dependence from claim 1, and in view of the reasons set forth above regarding amended claim 1, claims 4-6, 8, and 9 are also allowable over the cited art. Furthermore, the secondary reference Matthieu fails to cure the deficiencies of the primary reference Velicki. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejection of claims 4-6, 8, and 9 are respectfully requested.

As it is believed that all of the rejections set forth in the Office Action have been fully met, favorable reconsideration and allowance are earnestly solicited. If, however, for any reason the Examiner does not believe that such action can be taken at this time, it is respectfully requested that
the Examiner telephone Applicant's Attorney at (908) 654-5000 in order to overcome any additional objections which the Examiner might have.
All required fees are being paid via credit card. However, please charge any additional fees not already paid via credit card, and credit any overpayments to, our Deposit Account No. 12-1095.
